caption: Jumper cables from a running car are clamped onto a dead car's battery, and the dead car's dashboard lights come on.

sa.check: Jumper cables with clamps lead from a second car to the open engine bay of the first.
The clamps are fixed onto the dead car's battery terminals.
The dead car's dashboard lights come on.
The dashboard is dark before the clamps go on.
The order is clamps on, then lights.

pc.expect: The dashboard lights come on when the second clamp is seated on the battery, and only then.
pc.fail: Both clamps are on the battery and the dashboard stays dark to the end of the clip; or the dashboard lights while the clamps are still off the battery; or the lights come on with one clamp hanging loose beside its terminal.

pc.expect: Once lit the dashboard stays lit while the clamps stay on the terminals.
pc.fail: The dashboard goes dark again with the clamps still on; or the lights switch on and off with the clamps untouched; or a clamp springs off its terminal by itself.

pc.expect: The cable hangs slack from each clamp, and the clamps are rigid jaws that grip the terminal posts.
pc.fail: The cable stands rigid in the air or stretches like elastic; or a clamp bends like rubber around the post; or a clamp hangs on the post with its jaws still wide open.

pc.expect: The battery and the parts around it stay put as the clamps go on; the dead car does not move.
pc.fail: The battery slides in its tray with nothing touching it; or the bonnet swings by itself; or the dead car rolls or rocks as the clamps go on.

pc.expect: Two clamps on one battery; the clamps stay outside the battery casing; the cables stay continuous and the cars keep their shape.
pc.fail: A clamp passes into the battery casing; or a third clamp appears or one vanishes; or a cable splits or detaches; or the battery changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The cable colours, the battery's label and the engine bay stay the same.
pc.fail: A cable changes colour; or the battery's label changes; or engine parts change shape or place.

note: 'Running' has no visible sign the judge needs; the second car's engine is not judged. The battery and the dashboard are unlikely to share one view: S3 is judged on whatever view of the dead car's dashboard the clip gives, and P1 on the order of clamp seating and dashboard lighting as far as both are shown.
